reading.next: Greenhills first — it is the one shop I have now failed twice to explain, and the reading has changed under me: it is losing transactions, not basket, and the fall runs across every weekday rather than one bad day. That is a footfall or an opening-hours question, not a range question, and nothing in the sales data settles it. I'd ask the Greenhills manager what changed in the mall or the roster after 13 September, and I'd count the kiamoy shelf by hand: Kiamoy White nearly stopped selling there while king seedless and the premium pack rose in the same week, which is either a deliberate switch or a relabel nobody told us about. A hand count is the only way to know — the stock record has too many counts below zero to answer it. Magnolia second. It was the weakest shop yesterday against the same weekday by a wide margin and it is down again on the week — two readings pointing the same way, and I'd rather look at it this week than after a third. Then the shelf: Dikiam fell by half at Greenhills, the same too-thin-to-serve pattern I recorded a week ago. Say the word and I'll draft the AJI BARN order for the kiamoy and dikiam lines so we stop refilling only after they hit zero. The one structural fix: set low-stock levels, and clear the negative counts. Until both are done I can only ever tell you a line has already gone, never that it is about to.
reading.claim: We are down 4.5% on the week and every peso of it is fewer transactions
reading.caveat: The stock side cannot be trusted as read: 2,180 counts are below zero, the lowest at -78,291, and a count below zero is a broken record rather than an empty shelf — so a line shown as out of stock may simply be miscounted, and none of those quantities can be added up. Nobody has set a low-stock level on any product either, so a line is only ever seen the day it crosses to zero. On the sales side, product comparisons can't rank 122 of 500 lines: 66 sold in the earlier week and not this one, 44 are new, 12 had nothing to compare against. Purchase orders and transfers haven't moved since 18 September, so deliveries are invisible; vending stock is 47 days stale.
